_about: Country nerd facts for the 🤓 Nerd facts pop-up on Countries cards. Keyed by country name as in countries.json. Each fact: [label, text], kid-friendly, 160 characters max.
_verify: Written 2026-11-18, with populations rounded from 2024-25 estimates. Fact-checked 2026-11-20 (see FACT-CHECK.md).

Algeria: About 47 million people live in Algeria. That's more people than live in California, the biggest US state.
The Sahara covers more than 80% of Algeria. Its Tassili n'Ajjer plateau has thousands of ancient rock paintings.
Writer Albert Camus was born in Algeria and won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Angola: About 38 million people live in Angola. That's the 2nd most in Central Africa. It's about as many people as live in California.
The giant sable antelope, with huge curved horns, lives only in Angola and is a national symbol.
Kizomba, a smooth partner dance now loved around the world, comes from Angola.
Benin: About 14 million people live in Benin. That's about as many people as live in Pennsylvania.
Singer Angélique Kidjo, winner of several Grammy Awards, is from Benin.
Benin is famous for colorful appliqué cloth banners that tell stories with pictures.
Botswana: About 2.5 million people live in Botswana. That's about as many people as live in Chicago.
The Okavango River never reaches the sea. It spreads out into a giant delta and soaks into the Kalahari Desert.
Botswana's money is called the pula, which means 'rain,' because rain is so precious there.
Burkina Faso: About 23 million people live in Burkina Faso. That's about as many people as live in Florida.
The Grand Mosque of Bobo-Dioulasso is made of mud brick, with wooden poles sticking out of its walls.
Gold and cotton are Burkina Faso's biggest exports.
Burundi: About 14 million people live in Burundi. That's about as many people as live in Pennsylvania.
Lake Tanganyika, on Burundi's border, is the second-deepest lake in the world.
A small stream in Burundi is said to be the farthest-south source of the mighty Nile River.
Cabo Verde: About half a million people live in Cabo Verde. That's the fewest of any country in West Africa. It's about as many people as live in Miami.
Morna, a gentle and soulful style of music, is Cabo Verde's national music and a UNESCO treasure.
Pico do Fogo is a volcano, and families grow coffee and fruit inside its huge crater.
Cameroon: About 29 million people live in Cameroon. That's one of the most in Central Africa. It's about as many people as live in Texas.
Cameroon has more than 250 local languages, plus French and English as official languages.
Mount Cameroon is one of Africa's most active volcanoes, and runners race up it every year.
Central African Republic: About 5.5 million people live in the Central African Republic. That's about as many people as live in Colorado.
In Dzanga-Sangha park, hundreds of forest elephants gather in one big clearing to drink.
Almost everyone speaks Sango, along with French.
Chad: About 20 million people live in Chad. That's about as many people as live in New York State.
Chad's Bodélé Depression is the dustiest place on Earth. Its dust blows across the ocean and feeds the Amazon rainforest!
Zakouma National Park is famous for big herds of elephants and giraffes.
Comoros: About 850,000 people live in the Comoros. That's the 2nd fewest in East Africa. It's about as many people as live in San Francisco.
The coelacanth, a fish thought to be gone for millions of years, was found alive near the Comoros.
Mount Karthala, on the main island, has one of the biggest volcano craters in the world.
Republic of the Congo: About 6 million people live in the Republic of the Congo. That's about as many people as live in Colorado.
Its capital, Brazzaville, sits right across the Congo River from Kinshasa, another country's capital.
Congolese 'sapeurs' are famous for wearing super-stylish, colorful suits.
Democratic Republic of the Congo: About 110 million people live in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. That's the most of any country in Central Africa.
The Congo River is the deepest river in the world, more than 700 feet deep in places.
Congolese rumba music is so loved that UNESCO added it to its list of world treasures in 2021.
Ivory Coast (Côte d'Ivoire): About 31 million people live in Ivory Coast. That's one of the most in West Africa. It's about as many people as live in Texas.
French is the official language, and Abidjan is one of the biggest French-speaking cities in the world.
Coupé-décalé, a bouncy dance music style, was born among Ivorian DJs.
Djibouti: About 1.1 million people live in Djibouti. That's one of the fewest in East Africa. It's about as many people as live in Austin, Texas.
Lac Abbé has tall chimney-like rock towers that puff steam, while flamingos wade between them.
Whale sharks, the biggest fish in the sea, visit Djibouti's coast every winter.
Egypt: About 116 million people live in Egypt. That's the most of any country in North Africa. It's about three times as many people as California.
Koshari, a mix of rice, lentils, pasta and tomato sauce, is Egypt's national dish.
Ancient Egyptians made one of the first 365-day calendars.
Equatorial Guinea: About 1.9 million people live in Equatorial Guinea. That's the 2nd fewest in Central Africa. It's about as many people as live in Nebraska.
Its capital, Malabo, is on Bioko Island, not on the mainland.
Bioko Island is home to rare monkeys, like the drill, found in very few places.
Eritrea: About 3.5 million people live in Eritrea. That's about as many people as live in Los Angeles.
Asmara has a famous old gas station shaped like an airplane, the Fiat Tagliero.
The Dahlak Archipelago has more than 100 islands surrounded by coral reefs.
Eswatini: About 1.2 million people live in Eswatini. That's the fewest of any country in Southern Africa. It's about as many people as live in San Diego.
Eswatini is one of the smallest countries in Africa and one of the last kingdoms in the world.
Hlane Royal National Park protects rhinos, lions and elephants.
Ethiopia: About 130 million people live in Ethiopia. That's the most of any country in East Africa.
Ethiopia has its own calendar with 13 months, and it's about 7 years behind the one most countries use!
Injera, a spongy flatbread made from teff grain, is used as a plate and a spoon.
Gabon: About 2.5 million people live in Gabon. That's one of the fewest in Central Africa. It's about as many people as live in Chicago.
The mandrill, the biggest monkey in the world, with a bright red and blue face, lives in Gabon's forests.
Gabon created 13 national parks in 2002, protecting about a tenth of the country.
Gambia: About 2.8 million people live in the Gambia. That's one of the fewest in West Africa. It's about as many people as live in Chicago.
The Gambia is called 'the Smiling Coast of Africa.'
More than 500 kinds of birds have been spotted here, so birdwatchers love it.
Ghana: About 34 million people live in Ghana. That's one of the most in West Africa. It's about as many people as live in Texas.
Ghana's Adinkra symbols are printed on cloth, and each one stands for a saying or idea.
Kofi Annan, a leader of the United Nations who won the Nobel Peace Prize, was from Ghana.
Guinea: About 14.5 million people live in Guinea. That's about as many people as live in Pennsylvania.
Guinea is called the 'water tower of West Africa' because the Niger, Senegal and Gambia rivers start there.
Les Ballets Africains, Guinea's national dance company, has toured the whole world.
Guinea-Bissau: About 2.2 million people live in Guinea-Bissau. That's the 2nd fewest in West Africa. It's about as many people as live in Nebraska.
Gumbe is Guinea-Bissau's lively traditional music.
The Bijagós Archipelago has about 88 islands, and sea turtles nest on its beaches.
Kenya: About 56 million people live in Kenya. That's one of the most in East Africa. It's more people than live in California, the biggest US state.
Wangari Maathai started a movement that planted millions of trees, and she won the Nobel Peace Prize.
Swahili words like 'safari' (journey) and 'hakuna matata' (no worries) are spoken in Kenya.
Lesotho: About 2.3 million people live in Lesotho. That's one of the fewest in Southern Africa. It's about as many people as live in Chicago.
People wear colorful Basotho blankets, and the pointy Basotho hat appears on the flag.
Maletsunyane Falls drops more than 600 feet in one big leap.
Liberia: About 5.6 million people live in Liberia. That's about as many people as live in Colorado.
Liberia's flag looks like the US flag, but with just one star.
Sapo National Park is a huge rainforest home to rare pygmy hippos.
Libya: About 7.4 million people live in Libya. That's the fewest of any country in North Africa. It's about as many people as live in Arizona.
The old town of Ghadames, the 'pearl of the desert,' has covered streets that stay cool in the heat.
Libya's Sahara has some of the hottest and driest places on Earth.
Madagascar: About 31 million people live in Madagascar. That's about as many people as live in Texas.
Six kinds of baobab tree grow only in Madagascar, and some line the famous Avenue of the Baobabs.
The movie Madagascar starred a lion, a zebra, a giraffe and a hippo, animals that don't actually live there!
Malawi: About 21 million people live in Malawi. That's about as many people as live in New York State.
Lake Malawi covers about a fifth of the whole country.
The Gule Wamkulu dance, performed in giant masks, is a UNESCO world treasure.
Mali: About 24 million people live in Mali. That's about as many people as live in Florida.
Timbuktu was once a famous city of scholars, with hundreds of thousands of old handwritten books.
Singer Salif Keita, called the 'Golden Voice of Africa,' is from Mali.
Mauritania: About 5 million people live in Mauritania. That's about as many people as live in Alabama.
One of the longest trains in the world, about 1.5 miles long, carries iron ore across the Sahara here.
The desert town of Chinguetti has old family libraries full of handwritten books.
Mauritius: About 1.3 million people live in Mauritius. That's about as many people as live in San Diego.
The 'Blue Penny' stamp from Mauritius is one of the rarest stamps in the world.
From the air, sand flowing off its coast looks like an underwater waterfall.
Morocco: About 38 million people live in Morocco. That's about as many people as live in California.
Chefchaouen is a mountain town painted almost entirely blue.
Many famous movies have filmed their desert scenes at the studios in Ouarzazate.
Mozambique: About 34 million people live in Mozambique. That's about as many people as live in Texas.
Dugongs, gentle 'sea cows,' graze on seagrass around the Bazaruto islands.
Ilha de Moçambique, a little island town, gave the whole country its name.
Namibia: About 3 million people live in Namibia. That's the 2nd most in Southern Africa. It's about as many people as live in Iowa.
The Namib is thought to be the oldest desert in the world, about 55 million years old.
Namibia has more cheetahs than any other country.
Niger: About 27 million people live in Niger. That's about as many people as live in Texas.
Niger is home to West Africa's last wild giraffes, which wander near villages.
Agadez's Grand Mosque has a tall mud-brick tower that's hundreds of years old.
Nigeria: About 230 million people live in Nigeria. That's the most of any country in West Africa. It's about six times as many people as California.
Author Chinua Achebe wrote Things Fall Apart, one of the most-read books from Africa.
Afrobeats stars like Burna Boy and Wizkid come from Nigeria.
Rwanda: About 14 million people live in Rwanda. That's about as many people as live in Pennsylvania.
On the last Saturday of each month, Rwandans join Umuganda, a community clean-up day.
Plastic bags have been banned since 2008, making Rwanda one of Africa's cleanest countries.
São Tomé and Príncipe: About 230,000 people live in São Tomé and Príncipe. That's the fewest of any country in Central Africa. It's about as many people as live in Salt Lake City.
Pico Cão Grande is a giant needle-shaped rock tower poking out of the rainforest.
It's the second-smallest country in Africa.
Senegal: About 18.5 million people live in Senegal. That's about as many people as live in New York State.
Singer Youssou N'Dour is one of Africa's most famous musicians.
The African Renaissance Monument in Dakar is the tallest statue in Africa.
Seychelles: About 130,000 people live in Seychelles. That's the fewest of any country in East Africa. It's just a bit more than one giant football stadium can hold!
Its granite islands are some of the oldest ocean islands on Earth.
Aldabra Atoll is home to about 100,000 giant tortoises.
Sierra Leone: About 8.6 million people live in Sierra Leone. That's about as many people as live in New York City.
Its capital, Freetown, has one of the biggest natural harbors in the world.
The Tacugama Sanctuary cares for rescued chimpanzees, the national animal.
Somalia: About 19 million people live in Somalia. That's about as many people as live in New York State.
Somalia is called the 'Nation of Poets' because poetry is so loved there.
The Laas Geel caves have colorful rock paintings of cows that are thousands of years old.
South Africa: About 64 million people live in South Africa. That's the most of any country in Southern Africa.
The world's first human heart transplant was done in Cape Town in 1967.
Table Mountain in Cape Town is one of the oldest mountains on Earth.
South Sudan: About 12 million people live in South Sudan. That's about as many people as live in Ohio.
The Sudd is one of the biggest wetlands in the world.
Cattle are very important in South Sudan and appear in many songs and celebrations.
Sudan: About 50 million people live in Sudan. That's one of the most in North Africa. It's more people than live in California, the biggest US state.
The pyramids of Meroë have steep, pointy sides, different from Egypt's.
Ful medames, a hearty bean stew, is a favorite breakfast.
Tanzania: About 68 million people live in Tanzania. That's the 2nd most in East Africa. It's about twice as many people as California.
Lake Tanganyika is the longest freshwater lake in the world.
Freddie Mercury, the singer of the band Queen, was born on Zanzibar.
Togo: About 9.5 million people live in Togo. That's about as many people as live in Michigan.
Togo is very thin: only about 30 miles wide along its coast.
Togo is known for colorful wax-print fabrics sold in Lomé's huge market.
Tunisia: About 12 million people live in Tunisia. That's the 2nd fewest in North Africa. It's about as many people as live in Ohio.
Sidi Bou Said is a cliffside village painted white and bright blue.
Harissa, a spicy red chili paste, is a Tunisian favorite.
Uganda: About 50 million people live in Uganda. That's more people than live in California, the biggest US state.
The Rwenzori, the 'Mountains of the Moon,' have snow and glaciers near the equator.
Queen Elizabeth National Park has lions that climb trees and nap in the branches.
Zambia: About 21 million people live in Zambia. That's about as many people as live in New York State.
Every year about 10 million fruit bats fly into Kasanka park, one of the biggest animal migrations on Earth.
Lake Kariba, shared with Zimbabwe, is one of the biggest human-made lakes in the world.
Zimbabwe: About 17 million people live in Zimbabwe. That's about as many people as live in New York State.
Hwange National Park has one of Africa's biggest elephant herds.
Stone sculptures by Shona artists are famous around the world.
Afghanistan: About 42 million people live in Afghanistan. That's about as many people as live in California.
Kabuli pulao, rice cooked with carrots and raisins, is the national dish.
The Wakhan Corridor is a long, skinny strip of land that reaches all the way to China.
Armenia: About 3 million people live in Armenia. That's about as many people as live in Iowa.
Armenia has its own alphabet, created in the year 405 by a scholar named Mesrop Mashtots.
Armenia was the first country to make chess a school subject for kids.
Azerbaijan: About 10 million people live in Azerbaijan. That's about as many people as live in Michigan.
Azerbaijan has about half of all the mud volcanoes on Earth.
Mugham, Azerbaijan's traditional music, is a UNESCO world treasure.
Bahrain: About 1.6 million people live in Bahrain. That's the fewest of any country in the Middle East. It's about as many people as live in Philadelphia.
Bahrain hosts a Formula 1 race under bright floodlights in the desert.
Bahrain is a group of islands linked to Saudi Arabia by a 15-mile bridge and causeway.
Bangladesh: About 175 million people live in Bangladesh. That's the 8th most of any country in the world.
Cox's Bazar has one of the longest natural beaches in the world, about 75 miles long.
Muhammad Yunus won the Nobel Peace Prize for tiny loans that help people start small businesses.
Bhutan: About 800,000 people live in Bhutan. That's the 2nd fewest in South Asia. It's about as many people as live in San Francisco.
Bhutan's forests soak up more carbon than the country makes.
Brunei: About 460,000 people live in Brunei. That's the fewest of any country in Southeast Asia. It's about as many people as live in Miami.
The Sultan's palace is one of the biggest homes in the world, with about 1,800 rooms.
About 70% of Brunei is covered in rainforest.
Cambodia: About 17.5 million people live in Cambodia. That's about as many people as live in New York State.
Fish amok, fish steamed in banana leaves with coconut curry, is a national dish.
Tonlé Sap lake grows about five times bigger in the rainy season.
China: About 1.4 billion people live in China. That's the 2nd most in the world, just behind India. It's more than 35 times as many people as California.
Wild giant pandas live only in the mountains of China.
More people speak Mandarin Chinese as their first language than any other language.
Georgia: About 3.7 million people live in Georgia. That's about as many people as live in Los Angeles.
Georgia has its own alphabet, with 33 curly letters.
Georgian polyphonic singing, with many voices weaving together, is a UNESCO treasure.
India: About 1.45 billion people live in India. That's the most of any country in the world. It's more than 35 times as many people as California.
India makes more movies every year than any other country. Bollywood is in Mumbai.
Yoga began in India thousands of years ago.
Indonesia: About 280 million people live in Indonesia. That's the 4th most of any country in the world. It's about seven times as many people as California.
Indonesia has more active volcanoes than any other country.
Batik, cloth decorated with wax and dye patterns, is a famous Indonesian art.
Iran: About 90 million people live in Iran. That's one of the most in the Middle East.
Nowruz, the Persian New Year, starts on the first day of spring.
Isfahan's Naqsh-e Jahan Square is one of the biggest city squares in the world.
Iraq: About 46 million people live in Iraq. That's one of the most in the Middle East. It's more people than live in California, the biggest US state.
Ancient Mesopotamians counted in 60s, which is why an hour has 60 minutes.
Babylon, one of the most famous cities of the ancient world, was in Iraq.
Israel: About 10 million people live in Israel. That's about as many people as live in Michigan.
One of the first USB flash drives and the Waze navigation app were invented in Israel.
Falafel and hummus are everyday favorites.
Japan: About 124 million people live in Japan. That's the 2nd most in East Asia. It's about three times as many people as California.
Japan is made up of about 14,000 islands.
Instant noodles were invented in Japan in 1958.
Jordan: About 11.5 million people live in Jordan. That's about as many people as live in Ohio.
Jordan's red desert valleys played the planet Mars in the movie The Martian.
The Dead Sea, on Jordan's border, is the lowest place on land on Earth.
Kazakhstan: About 20 million people live in Kazakhstan. That's the 2nd most in Central Asia. It's about as many people as live in New York State.
Charyn Canyon is nicknamed the little brother of the Grand Canyon.
The capital, Astana, has a tower shaped like a tree holding a golden egg.
Kuwait: About 4.9 million people live in Kuwait. That's one of the fewest in the Middle East. It's about as many people as live in Alabama.
The Kuwaiti dinar is one of the most valuable currencies in the world.
Kuwait has no rivers at all.
Kyrgyzstan: About 7 million people live in Kyrgyzstan. That's one of the fewest in Central Asia. It's about as many people as live in Arizona.
Issyk-Kul is one of the biggest mountain lakes in the world, and it never freezes.
The Epic of Manas is one of the longest poems ever told, with about half a million lines.
Laos: About 7.7 million people live in Laos. That's about as many people as live in Arizona.
Laos is the only Southeast Asian country with no coastline.
The Plain of Jars is covered with thousands of giant stone jars from long ago.
Lebanon: About 5.8 million people live in Lebanon. That's about as many people as live in Colorado.
Lebanon's name comes from an old word for 'white,' after its snowy mountains.
Byblos is one of the oldest cities on Earth, and the word 'Bible' comes from its name.
Malaysia: About 35 million people live in Malaysia. That's about as many people as live in California.
The rafflesia, the biggest flower in the world, blooms in Malaysia's rainforests.
Orangutans, whose name means 'person of the forest,' live in Malaysian Borneo.
Maldives: About half a million people live in the Maldives. That's the fewest of any country in South Asia. It's about as many people as live in Miami.
Some Maldives beaches glow blue at night, lit up by tiny sea plankton.
The Maldives is famous for hotel rooms built on stilts over the water.
Mongolia: About 3.5 million people live in Mongolia. That's the fewest of any country in East Asia. It's about as many people as live in Los Angeles.
The first dinosaur eggs ever recognized by scientists were found in Mongolia's Gobi Desert in the 1920s.
The Naadam festival features wrestling, horse racing and archery.
Myanmar: About 54 million people live in Myanmar. That's more people than live in California, the biggest US state.
Fishermen on Inle Lake row their boats with one leg.
Many people wear thanaka, a yellow paste made from tree bark, on their faces as sunscreen.
Nepal: About 30 million people live in Nepal. That's about as many people as live in Texas.
Nepal is the only country whose flag isn't a rectangle. It's two stacked triangles!
Chitwan National Park is home to one-horned rhinos and Bengal tigers.
North Korea: About 26 million people live in North Korea. That's about as many people as live in Florida.
Mount Kumgang, the 'Diamond Mountain,' is famous for its jagged rocky peaks.
Kimchi, spicy fermented cabbage, is eaten with almost every meal.
Oman: About 5 million people live in Oman. That's about as many people as live in Alabama.
Wadi Shab has turquoise pools you can swim through to a waterfall hidden in a cave.
Green sea turtles come ashore to nest on Ras al Jinz beach.
Pakistan: About 250 million people live in Pakistan. That's the 2nd most in South Asia.
Three huge mountain ranges meet in Pakistan: the Himalayas, the Karakoram and the Hindu Kush.
Malala Yousafzai became the youngest Nobel Peace Prize winner ever, at age 17.
Palestine: About 5.5 million people live in Palestine. That's about as many people as live in Colorado.
Jericho is one of the oldest cities in the world, and Bethlehem is a famous old town.
Musakhan, roasted chicken on flatbread with onions and sumac, is a national dish.
Philippines: About 115 million people live in the Philippines. That's the 2nd most in Southeast Asia. It's about three times as many people as California.
The Chocolate Hills are more than 1,200 round hills that turn brown in the dry season.
The tarsier, a tiny primate with giant eyes, lives in the Philippines.
Qatar: About 3 million people live in Qatar. That's the 2nd fewest in the Middle East. It's about as many people as live in Iowa.
At Khor Al Adaid, the 'Inland Sea,' giant sand dunes run right into the sea.
Doha's Museum of Islamic Art sits on its own little island.
Saudi Arabia: About 35 million people live in Saudi Arabia. That's about as many people as live in California.
Saudi Arabia is the biggest country in the world with no permanent rivers.
Kabsa, spiced rice with chicken or lamb, is the national dish.
Singapore: About 6 million people live in Singapore. That's one of the fewest in Southeast Asia. It's about as many people as live in Colorado.
Selling chewing gum is banned in Singapore to help keep the streets clean.
Singapore's airport has the Jewel, a giant indoor waterfall surrounded by a forest.
South Korea: About 51 million people live in South Korea. That's more people than live in California, the biggest US state.
Taekwondo, a martial art with high kicks, comes from Korea.
South Korea has some of the fastest internet in the world.
Sri Lanka: About 22 million people live in Sri Lanka. That's one of the fewest in South Asia. It's about as many people as live in Florida.
Sigiriya, the 'Lion Rock,' has the ruins of a palace on top of a giant rock.
Sri Lanka had the world's first woman prime minister, Sirimavo Bandaranaike, in 1960.
Syria: About 24 million people live in Syria. That's about as many people as live in Florida.
One of the world's first alphabets was written in Ugarit, an ancient city in Syria.
Kibbeh and fattoush salad are favorite Syrian foods.
Taiwan: About 23 million people live in Taiwan. That's the 2nd fewest in East Asia. It's about as many people as live in Florida.
The Formosan black bear, with a white V on its chest, is a national symbol.
At the Pingxi Lantern Festival, thousands of glowing sky lanterns float into the night.
Tajikistan: About 10.5 million people live in Tajikistan. That's about as many people as live in Michigan.
Ismoil Somoni Peak, its tallest mountain, is more than 24,000 feet high.
Tajik is a close cousin of the Persian language.
Thailand: About 72 million people live in Thailand. That's about twice as many people as California.
Bangkok's full name in Thai is one of the longest city names in the world.
Songkran, the Thai New Year, is celebrated with giant water fights in the streets.
Timor-Leste: About 1.4 million people live in Timor-Leste. That's the 2nd fewest in Southeast Asia. It's about as many people as live in San Diego.
Timor-Leste has two official languages: Tetum and Portuguese.
Tais, colorful hand-woven cloth, is a UNESCO world treasure.
Türkiye (Turkey): About 86 million people live in Türkiye. That's one of the most in the Middle East. It's about twice as many people as California.
Istanbul is a giant city that sits on two continents: Europe and Asia.
In Cappadocia, hot air balloons float over rock towers nicknamed 'fairy chimneys.'
Turkmenistan: About 7 million people live in Turkmenistan. That's one of the fewest in Central Asia. It's about as many people as live in Arizona.
The Karakum Desert covers about 80% of the country.
Turkmen carpets are so important that carpet patterns appear on the flag.
United Arab Emirates: About 11 million people live in the United Arab Emirates. That's about as many people as live in Ohio.
In 2021 the UAE's Hope probe reached Mars, the first Arab mission to another planet.
Abu Dhabi's Sheikh Zayed Mosque has one of the biggest hand-knotted carpets in the world.
Uzbekistan: About 37 million people live in Uzbekistan. That's the most of any country in Central Asia. It's about as many people as live in California.
Uzbekistan is one of only two countries surrounded by countries that also have no coast.
Round non bread is stamped with pretty patterns before it's baked in clay ovens.
Vietnam: About 101 million people live in Vietnam. That's one of the most in Southeast Asia.
Son Doong is the biggest cave in the world, with its own jungle and clouds inside.
Water puppetry, with puppets dancing across a pond, is a Vietnamese art.
Yemen: About 40 million people live in Yemen. That's about as many people as live in California.
Socotra Island has umbrella-shaped trees and plants found nowhere else on Earth.
Sanaa's old houses are decorated with white patterns that look like gingerbread icing.
Albania: About 2.7 million people live in Albania. That's about as many people as live in Chicago.
The Blue Eye is a bright blue spring so clear you can see deep down into the water.
Traditionally, many Albanians nod to say 'no' and shake their heads to say 'yes.'
Andorra: About 80,000 people live in Andorra. That's one of the fewest in Southern Europe. They could all fit inside one giant football stadium!
Andorra has two princes at once: the President of France and a bishop from Spain.
Austria: About 9.2 million people live in Austria. That's about as many people as live in Michigan.
The snow globe was invented in Vienna around 1900.
The Vienna Boys' Choir has been singing for more than 500 years.
Belarus: About 9.2 million people live in Belarus. That's about as many people as live in Michigan.
Belarus has more than 10,000 lakes, so it's nicknamed the 'Land of Blue Lakes.'
Painter Marc Chagall, famous for his dreamy, colorful art, was born in Belarus.
Belgium: About 11.8 million people live in Belgium. That's about as many people as live in Ohio.
The saxophone was invented by a Belgian named Adolphe Sax.
Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French and German.
Bosnia and Herzegovina: About 3.2 million people live in Bosnia and Herzegovina. That's about as many people as live in Iowa.
Burek, a flaky spiral pastry filled with meat or cheese, is a favorite.
The Una River is famous for its emerald-green water and waterfalls.
Bulgaria: About 6.4 million people live in Bulgaria. That's one of the fewest in Eastern Europe. It's about as many people as live in Colorado.
The Cyrillic alphabet, used by millions of people today, was developed in Bulgaria long ago.
Each March, Bulgarians wear red-and-white martenitsa bracelets to welcome spring.
Croatia: About 3.9 million people live in Croatia. That's about as many people as live in Los Angeles.
The spotted Dalmatian dog is named after Croatia's Dalmatia region.
Dubrovnik's old town was a filming spot for Star Wars: The Last Jedi.
